articles.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Trump says he offered UFC CEO Dana White press secretary job
articles.excerpt: Kayleigh McEnany hosts a discussion on the pressure of serving as White House press secretary with Chad Gilmartin, Harrison Fields and Jalen Drummond. President Donald Trump states he is in no hurry t...
articles.body_text:
Kayleigh McEnany hosts a discussion on the pressure of serving as White House press secretary with Chad Gilmartin, Harrison Fields and Jalen Drummond. President Donald Trump states he is in no hurry to name a successor. The panel shares insider details about handling the press briefings.

President Donald Trump said Saturday he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House press secretary job, proposing a team of mixed martial arts stars to help defend his administration against political opponents.

Shortly after Trump published his post, White shared a photo on his Instagram Story of himself standing at the White House press podium with the caption, "On to the next chapter." He also shared Trump’s Truth Social post announcing the offer.

The Nov. 7 Truth Social post paired the proposed offer with a roster of fighters and an image collage. It did not establish that White had accepted the position, and it was not immediately clear whether Trump intended the proposal seriously.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote.

DANA WHITE SAYS 'I DON'T GIVE A S---' IF TRUMP FRIENDSHIP COSTS HIM BUSINESS, 250TH EVENT WAS TRUMP'S IDEA

The president named Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and Amanda Nunes as prospective assistants, while acknowledging that some were not American. He also listed "Kayla Harris," apparently referring to UFC fighter and two-time Olympic judo gold medalist Kayla Harrison.

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump added.

President Donald Trump and UFC President and CEO Dana White are introduced during UFC Freedom 250 at the White House on June 14, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

The post comes amid turnover in the White House’s senior ranks and weeks after the departure of Trump’s most recent press secretary.

Fox News Digital reported Oct. 16 that Katie Zacharia was leaving the position following her debut. Trump had announced her selection Oct. 9 to succeed Karoline Leavitt, who left in August. ABC News reported that Zacharia began work Oct. 12 and was transitioning out of the role that Friday.

Asked Oct. 23 about finding another press secretary, Trump told reporters, "No, nothing much. We’re in no rush."

Separately, the White House announced Friday that Stephen Miller would succeed Susie Wiles as chief of staff. That announcement confirmed a personnel change; Trump’s Saturday appeal to White left the proposed press secretary arrangement unresolved.

UFC'S DANA WHITE SAYS 'YOU'D BE SHOCKED' TO LEARN WHO ACTUALLY SUPPORTS TRUMP IN THE SHADOWS

U.S. President Donald Trump and UFC President and CEO Dana White walk out of the White House onto the South Lawn for the UFC Freedom 250 fight on June 14, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

White and Trump have a relationship stretching back decades, rooted partly in Trump’s support for UFC when the promotion was working to establish itself.

Trump hosted UFC events in Atlantic City as early as 2001, according to Sports Business Journal. White later became a prominent supporter of Trump’s presidential campaigns and spoke during his 2024 election-night victory celebration.

White also introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, describing their long friendship and praising Trump’s resilience.

Their relationship carried into Trump’s second term. The president attended UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn on June 14, 2026. Official White House photographs documented Trump and White walking through the building together to attend the event.

White has previously downplayed the prospect of entering politics himself.

President Donald J. Trump and UFC President Dana White watch the UFC lightweight championship fight during the UFC Freedom 250 event on the South Lawn at the White House in Washington, D.C., on June 14, 2026. (Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC)

"I have no personal political aspirations," he told Sports Business Journal in November 2024 when asked about a potential role in Trump’s incoming administration.

That statement preceded Saturday’s post by two years and does not establish White’s response to the latest proposal.

OutKick has reached out to the White House and UFC for comment.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Liberal podcasters apologize after laughing at joke about digging up Charlie Kirk's body
articles.excerpt:
Podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan are facing anger from political commentators after they laughed at a joke about digging up Charlie Kirk's body. (Getty Images)

Podcasters Jennifer Welc...
articles.body_text:
Podcast hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan are facing anger from political commentators after they laughed at a joke about digging up Charlie Kirk's body. (Getty Images)

Podcasters Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan drew criticism from political commentators after laughing at a social media post about exhuming the body of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. The two issued an apology on Saturday.

During Thursday's episode of Welch's "I've Had It" podcast, the two women laughed as they read social media reactions to Democrats' victories in the 2026 midterm elections. Several posts mocked conservative positions on issues including abortion, vaccines and LGBTQ+ policies.

"Somebody posted, ‘I don’t care if you celibate or abstinent. Grab the nearest person available and do your worst. Abortion’s on me,’" Welch said, reading from the social media posts.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan attend the 37th GLAAD Media Awards at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, Calif., on March 5, 2026. (Billboard via Getty Images)

The pair continued to laugh as they read other social media reactions mocking Republicans following the party's midterm election losses.

"You can't even fathom the pronouns we're going to invent," Welch read while laughing. "You can't even pronounce them."

The podcast host praised the writers of the various posts, calling the jokesters "patriots" and insisting that "these people make me patriotic."

Welch further broke out into laughter while reading another post aloud: "We're digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again."

'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL

Charlie Kirk throws hats to the crowd after arriving at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

On Saturday, the two hosts apologized via a post on Instagram.

"On Thursday’s show, we laughed at a joke about Charlie Kirk. It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize," the statement read. "Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence. We’ve long supported common-sense gun safety reform."

"To that end, we’ve made a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in America," the statement continued. "We’ll keep using our platforms to fight for the safety of all Americans."

During Thursday's episode, after laughing at the post, the hosts said, "No comment," before asserting without presenting evidence that Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Kirk, supported President Donald Trump.

DEMOCRATIC STUDENT GROUP TO PROTEST CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL AT CAMPUS WHERE HE WAS KILLED

"Other than he was shot by somebody that was super MAGA," Sullivan said.

"He was shot by a MAGA person," Welch said, adding, "White person, White MAGA family."

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

Far-left podcast star Jennifer Welch has emerged as a darling of the liberal media. (Bryan Bedder/Getty Images for GLAAD)

While Robinson and his family lived in Utah’s Washington County, a deep red county where 75% of residents voted to send President Donald Trump back to the White House, Fox News Digital previously reported that Utah Voter Registration records showed that Robinson is unaffiliated with a political party and did not vote in the past two general elections.

Several commentators criticized the hosts' remarks on social media.

PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST

"In all of their hatred and blood thirst, these ghouls seriously consider themselves morally superior to you," conservative activist Riley Gaines said in an X post.

"They will celebrate your death, laugh uncontrollably, and still be fully convinced they're the 'good guys,'" influencer Collin Rugg posted.

Media Research Center President David Bozell also criticized the hosts, telling Fox News Digital, "If Madison Ave. would stop sponsoring gutter trash, gutter trash would go out of business."

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff also criticized Welch and Sullivan's remarks.

BOBBY BURACK: ONLINE HATE IS WINNING, FROM PAT MCAFEE TO EVERYDAY AMERICANS AND YOUNG CHILDREN

"As a Democrat, it is frustrating to watch Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan get treated like voices for the Democratic Party when so much of their own brand is railing against Democrats," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "Have either of them persuaded a single person to vote for a Democrat?"

"Then, after Democrats just delivered historic wins and a massive blue wave, they say something this offensive and irresponsible and suddenly the story is about them instead," he added. "They are not helping Democrats. They are hijacking the attention Democrats actually earned at the ballot box."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Welch and Sullivan did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Deirdre Heavey contributed to this report.

Julia Bonavita is a media and culture writer for Fox News Digital, and a Fox Flight Team drone pilot. You can follow her at @juliabonavita13 on all platforms and send story tips to julia.bonavita@fox.com.

articles.title: Yemeni gov’t forces report advances as Houthis say deadly strikes hit Sanaa
articles.excerpt:
Yemeni government forces say they have repelled Houthi assaults in Marib, as the armed group said strikes on a village in Sanaa province had killed at least 27 people.

In a statement on Saturday, gov...
articles.body_text:
Yemeni government forces say they have repelled Houthi assaults in Marib, as the armed group said strikes on a village in Sanaa province had killed at least 27 people.

In a statement on Saturday, government forces said troops backed by warplanes and drones had fought for hours to halt Houthi advances in Marib province, destroying fortifications and combat equipment.

It said troops were also pushing into Houthi-held areas of al-Jawf province, where fighting entered a third consecutive day as part of the “Dawn of Yemen” operation launched more than a month ago by the internationally recognised government, to take control of territory from Houthi fighters.

In a separate statement, government forces spokesman, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, said the army had carried out 875 attacks on Houthi positions on Saturday, “neutralising” about 130 Houthi commanders and fighters and destroying or disabling 50 vehicles and missile launchers.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.

Also on Saturday, a series of strikes killed at least 27 people and wounded about 30 others in Sanaa province, the Houthi-run ⁠Saba news ⁠agency reported.

Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesman for the Sanaa-based Ministry of Health, said the attacks struck al-Shariya village, north of the capital. He said most of the casualties were women and children.

The Iran-backed Houthis – also known as Ansar Allah, Arabic for Supporters of God – blamed the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government forces for the attack. The President of the armed group’s Supreme Political Council, Field Marshal Mahdi al-Mashat, vowed to “avenge” the attack.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have not commented on the reported strikes.

The incident comes a day after the Houthis and Yemen’s government traded blame over a separate attack that killed civilians at a market in Taiz.

Reporting from Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said the Houthis put the civilian death toll from the past two days at 55, blaming Saudi air strikes, while Yemeni government officials have held the Houthis responsible for most of the casualties.

“Two narratives are blaming each other and pointing the finger at each other, while this is taking a toll on civilian casualties,” Mawry said.

As fighting continues in Yemen, the Houthis separately claimed to have launched six attacks on Saudi targets using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones, but did not say when the attacks were carried out.

The group said it had targeted King Khalid international airport and oil facilities in Riyadh, an oil site in Khurais, an oil pumping station in Dawadmi, a National Guard camp in Najran and what it described as Saudi troop gatherings in Yemen’s al-Jawf and Marib provinces.

Colonel Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the Saudi-backed coalition supporting Yemen’s government forces, said early on Saturday that they had shot down a Houthi ballistic missile over the Riyadh region.

articles.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
articles.excerpt:
The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who p...
articles.body_text:
The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details.

President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated" following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel.

Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon.

Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders.

The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies.

As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams.

Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil.

Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest

A US State Department statement about its multi-million dollar reward said it was offering the money for information about the Iranian programme, including "facilities, equipment and associated personnel".

It said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA [the International Atomic Energy Agency] on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like [nuclear] centrifuges".

Centrifuges are needed to produce enriched uranium, which can be used to make reactor fuel for civilian use but also for nuclear weapons if enriched to around 90% purity or higher.

There had been mounting speculation that the US might resume significant strikes in Iran after the midterm elections, though Trump told reporters, prior to the polls, that he was in "no rush" to do so.

In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, the president also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump said.

The president has repeatedly threatened to bomb the suspected underground site on previous occasions.

However, both Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have said public opposition to the war on Iran fuelled heavy losses for their Republican Party in this week's midterm elections, which has led to speculation the White House may no longer seek an escalation in the conflict.

On Friday, Trump insisted that Iran was keen to end the eight-month conflict with the US, stressing the damage to Tehran's economy and military.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that both sides were "reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented" and that it remained hopeful of a deal being agreed.

Iranian negotiators had discussed with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days once the US met its seven conditions.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

articles.title: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
articles.excerpt:
Children were among the injured people seen being carried into a nearby hospital

Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been kill...
articles.body_text:
Children were among the injured people seen being carried into a nearby hospital

Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plan landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

articles.title: Certain sleep habits could offer clues to hidden type of depression, scientists say
articles.excerpt:
Metabolic health expert Jim LaValle explains how chronic stress, inadequate sleep and everyday dietary choices can affect blood sugar regulation and contribute to insulin resistance.

A person's sleep...
articles.body_text:
Metabolic health expert Jim LaValle explains how chronic stress, inadequate sleep and everyday dietary choices can affect blood sugar regulation and contribute to insulin resistance.

A person's sleep habits may help identify a newly proposed subtype of depression linked to the body's internal clock.

In a study of 11,380 Australian adults with a history of depression, about 23% met researchers' criteria for what they called "circadian depression."

The profile included at least three of six features: being an evening person, waking up feeling very tired, sleeping longer during the worst periods of depression, experiencing seasonal changes, having a later midpoint between falling asleep and waking up, and experiencing "social jetlag," a large shift in sleep timing between workdays and days off.

The seasonal changes could involve sleep, mood, activity, appetite, weight or energy.

THE DAYTIME HABIT THAT COULD TRANSFORM YOUR SLEEP, ACCORDING TO NEW STUDY

The study, published on Oct. 20 in The British Journal of Psychiatry, could eventually help guide more personalized care for patients with depression, according to the researchers.

"Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them," first author Emiliana Tonini, Ph.D., from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Centre, said in a statement.

Researchers are studying whether disrupted sleep-wake rhythms may help identify a proposed subtype of depression. (iStock)

The label, however, is not a formal diagnosis and needs independent replication and further study, the researchers noted.

People in the circadian group reported an earlier onset of depression and more severe symptoms than those who did not meet the criteria. They were also more likely to report weight gain during depressive episodes.

They also reported poorer responses and more side effects with two common classes of antidepressants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs).

POPULAR SLEEP AIDS BEFORE SURGERY COULD PREVENT PAINKILLER DEPENDENCE LATER

Participants reported how well their medications worked, but the study did not explain why some were less effective and did not test treatments aimed at adjusting the body’s internal clock.

Researchers said light exposure, regular sleep schedules and melatonin-related approaches warrant further study.

The proposed circadian profile includes features such as waking very tired, oversleeping during depression and being an evening person. (iStock)

Dr. Ian Hickie, a study co-author and professor of psychiatry at the University of Sydney, said the proposed profile "cuts across existing historic subtypes" of depression, most commonly atypical and bipolar depression, because they share features such as low energy and oversleeping.

COMMON GYM SUPPLEMENT COULD HELP FIGHT DEPRESSION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

Atypical depression can also involve weight gain, while bipolar depression refers to depressive episodes in people with bipolar disorder, which also involves periods of unusually elevated or irritable mood and increased energy.

"We define circadian only by sleep-wake and circadian features," Hickie told Fox News Digital.

For some people with this profile, Hickie said sleep-wake disruption may be more than a symptom of depression. "This type of circadian disturbance is not simply a consequence, but the underlying cause," he wrote.

The study itself, however, could not establish whether body-clock disruption caused depression or resulted from it.

Staying up late or struggling to wake up does not, by itself, mean someone has depression, the researchers noted. (iStock)

Staying up late or having trouble waking does not necessarily indicate depression. Participants had already reported depression, which in some cases was severe, recurring or long-lasting.

Participants in the circadian group also reported more manic-like experiences. John Puls, a psychotherapist and adjunct professor at Florida Atlantic University, said those symptoms could help explain their reported response to antidepressants.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"SSRIs are not meant to treat these more significant mental health symptoms that go far beyond depressive symptoms," Puls, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "In fact, some SSRIs can actually worsen manic symptoms, which lead to poor sleep."

There were several limitations to the study, the researchers acknowledged.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Participants reported their own sleep patterns and treatment experiences, and the cross-sectional analysis didn't show whether sleep disruption preceded or followed depressive symptoms.

All participants were of European ancestry, so the findings may not apply to other populations.

Researchers used six sleep-related features to identify the proposed circadian depression profile, including having social jetlag and being an evening person. (iStock)

Jillian Amodio, a Maryland-based psychotherapist and founder of Moms For Mental Health, cautioned against using the findings as "a benchmark for treating each person in the same way."

"Biological, environmental, social and psychological factors all need to be accounted for," Amodio, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

Researchers should examine more populations, including people who work night shifts, and account for differences in time zones and seasons, according to Amodio.

The study was led by researchers at the University of Sydney and QIMR Berghofer Medical Research Institute, with co-authors from institutions in Australia, the U.K. and the U.S.

Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government
articles.excerpt:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked former army chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over his rival Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Herzog communicated his...
articles.body_text:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked former army chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over his rival Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Herzog communicated his decision to Eisenkot on Saturday evening and will formally hand him the mandate at a ceremony on Sunday, a statement from the president’s spokesperson said.

This comes after Herzog held consultations with all political parties this week, to decide who he would grant the chance to form a government after neither side secured a majority in the October 27 general election.

Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, was recommended by parties representing 67 lawmakers as opposed to 46 for Netanyahu’s bloc, the statement said.

Eisenkot will have 28 days – with a possible 14-day extension – to build a coalition that holds at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, the minimum threshold for a government.

In the October election, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

The decision on Saturday came hours after Netanyahu warned that a government formed by opposition parties with the support of Arab-led parties would lead to Israel’s collapse.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

articles.title: Nicolas Cage walks back 'homeless' claims after $10M Malibu mansion sinkhole disaster

Nicolas Cage walked back claims he was "a little bit homeless" months after a sinkhole engulfed his $10.5 million Malibu mansion.

The "ConAir" star admitted earlier this week that he was adapting to a unique housing situation following September's disaster where severe coastal erosion impacted his beachfront abode.

Cage, 62, explained that he got carried away in describing his property problems while "riffing with a very good interviewer" at Comic Con over the weekend.

NICOLAS CAGE'S MALIBU BEACHFRONT HOME DAMAGED AFTER DRIVEWAY COLLAPSES INTO MASSIVE SINKHOLE

Nicolas Cage claimed he was "a little bit homeless" during an appearance at Comic Con. (Chelsea Guglielmino)

While appearing at the L.A. event, Cage divulged that upcoming Halloween plans were a little tricky due to the sinkhole situation.

"I’m currently a little bit homeless," he said, per Page Six. "Something happened to my house in Malibu so I’m just sort of living in hotels, so I don’t have normal trick-or-treaters I would like to enjoy tonight."

NICHOLAS CAGE TURNED DOWN PARTS IN TWO BIG FRANCHISE MOVIES FOR ROLES HE THOUGHT WERE BETTER

The "Face/Off" actor revealed he would instead take his four-year-old daughter, August, trick-or-treating in nearby Santa Monica before tuning into Stanley Kubrick's classic, "The Shining."

Cage's beachfront home was damaged due to coastal erosion spurred by September's Hurricane Marie, which formed in the Pacific Ocean and generated massive waves in addition to high tides.

Nicolas Cage's beachfront home in Malibu was damaged in September due to coastal erosion from Hurricane Marie. (Getty Images)

Evacuations were issued for more than 30 homes on the private road near the west end of the affluent community, with the city explaining that the properties were unsafe due to "the loss of access for Fire and Sheriff’s personnel to respond to medical, fire or law enforcement emergencies."

Cage clarified with the Associated Press Wednesday that his words were taken out of context.

"I went to Comic Con and I was riffing with a very good interviewer and he just had to ask, because it was Halloween night, 'What are you doing for Halloween?'" he said. "Now, when I said that, I meant my house is not available for trick or treaters."

"Now, I have to watch my words so much to the letter. We’re content. We’re fine. We’re not destitute. We’re okay."

He added, "I was just meaning that the house is not available for decorations and for candy to hand out to the children, which I like to do because I like Halloween."

The "National Treasure" star purchased the 4,000-square-foot home in 2024 for $10.5 million, according to Realtor.com.

Unfortunately, that headline had to be deleted. You can blame Tiffany Stratton for that.

Tiffany Stratton celebrates her win during Crown Jewel at The Venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Nov. 7, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

Green secured the victory initially after Morgan had sent her Judgment Day stablemates, Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez to the back. She said she didn’t need their help to beat Green. articles.title: What we know so far after Polish gunman opens fire in Krakow main square
articles.excerpt: At least six people have been killed and several others injured after a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Here's everythi...
articles.body_text:
At least six people have been killed and several others injured after a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Here's everything we know so far.

The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city.

Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car".

Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard.

A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured.

People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further  massacre, officials said.

The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times.

The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself.

Moment police officer appears to shoot Krakow suspect

Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor.

City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.

The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for possible explosive devices, police say. Residents of nearby buildings are being evacuated while the operation is under way.

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a foreign national.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while  detaining the attacker.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name.

The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier.

"Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added.

Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.

A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police.

The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.

Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.

Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.

"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."

Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.

She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday.

Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances".

Krakow Mayor Łukasz Gibała has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, November 11.

President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events".

US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack".

The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland".

articles.title: More than 140,000 rally as new protests against rising costs sweep France
articles.excerpt:
Tens of thousands of people have protested across France for a fourth consecutive weekend, in another show of anger against the government.

About 146,000 people rallied across the country to protest ...
articles.body_text:
Tens of thousands of people have protested across France for a fourth consecutive weekend, in another show of anger against the government.

About 146,000 people rallied across the country to protest against the rising cost of living on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the Ministry of the Interior said.

Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital.

The demonstrations come just days after an estimated 575,000 people took part in a rally organised by trade unions.

About 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country on Saturday, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warning that authorities would be “ready and waiting” for anyone engaging in rioting or looting.

Clashes broke out between police and some protesters in the capital, Paris, despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks.

Footage posted online by the CLPRESS news agency showed police charging at protesters and using tear gas in an attempt to disperse the crowds. A police officer was also seen hitting a protester with a baton.

Police said a group of 200 individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a rubbish bin in a square in Paris, the AFP news agency reported.

In the southeastern city of Lyon, police also fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre who were blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering.

Reporting from the French capital, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said people working in a variety of jobs attended Saturday’s demonstrations in support of the student-led movement.

“I spoke to one railway worker who told me it was really important to be here today. He said not only was it important to protest against the cost of living, but that it was also important to support young people,” Butler said.

“There is no doubt that the trade unions, who’ve been weakened in recent years, really feel there is a sense of momentum,” she said. “Many of the workers that I’ve been speaking to say this is their time to really press the government for higher salaries and better facilities.”

The demonstrations in France began in September over poor conditions and a lack of resources at French high schools. The protests later expanded to encompass a host of grievances, linked to worsening living standards. The movement continues to be led by France’s students, but people of all ages have been taking part.

This weekend’s protests take place against the backdrop of France’s upcoming presidential election, due to be held in April. Polls put far-right candidate Marine Le Pen of the National Rally first, followed by far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon of the France Unbowed party.

Melenchon unveiled his programme on Saturday to some 17,000 supporters and promised to do the opposite of incumbent President Emmanuel Macron.

He pledged to stimulate the economy by capitalising on consumer spending and “through billions [of euros] that already exist”, adding that these savings “must be channelled towards our country’s ecological and social needs”.

articles.title: Richard Lloyd, founding member and guitarist of punk band Television, dies aged 75
articles.excerpt:
Known for sophisticated musical style in band that played significant role in emerging 1970s punk rock movement

Richard Lloyd, known for his sophisticated musical style as a founding member and guita...
articles.body_text:
Known for sophisticated musical style in band that played significant role in emerging 1970s punk rock movement

Richard Lloyd, known for his sophisticated musical style as a founding member and guitarist for the influential punk band Television, has died at the age of 75.

His family confirmed that Lloyd died Saturday morning at his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee. “His loving wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays were with him at the end,” his family said in a statement to Rolling Stone.

According to his family, Lloyd’s death was caused by cholangiocarcinoma, a form of bile duct cancer that he was diagnosed with in March 2026.

A crowdfunding campaign had revealed that Lloyd had developed tumors in his liver and, crucially, there was one that could not be surgically removed.

Television, which formed in 1973, played a significant role in the emerging punk rock movement that grew up around CBGB, the legendary former music venue on the Bowery in New York City. The group was among the earliest punk acts to perform at the downtown venue, which had previously focused mainly on country and bluegrass music.

During a 2007 interview, Lloyd reflected on his role in shaping the club’s history, declaring: “CBGB’s is the most famous rock ‘n’ roll club to have ever existed and I fucking created it! I was the invisible force behind it.”

Television recorded just two studio albums during its peak in the late 1970s. The band’s first album, released in 1977, was Marquee Moon, which has since earned widespread recognition as a landmark recording. Rolling Stone ranked it No 107 on its 2023 list of the 500 greatest albums of all time. The record is still considered one of the most influential guitar-driven albums in rock history.

In a 2005 review, the Guardian described his performance, writing that “Lloyd’s guitar was the louder in a lopsided sound mix, so it was impossible to overlook the amount of ground he was covering. Crisp, crunchy chords, dextrous fills and torrential Van Halen-style solos tumbled from his fingers.”

articles.title: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
articles.excerpt:
Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technology

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic co...
articles.body_text:
Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technology

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing new technology first to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska as the Trump administration presses ahead with updating the country’s ageing aviation infrastructure.

The systems are now online at the Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and the Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska, with five additional regional airports slated to receive the technology next.

The digital towers use advanced camera systems and digital displays to give air traffic controllers a continuous, 360-degree view of airport operations, including runways, taxiways and surrounding airspace, according to the agency.

The FAA maintains that the technology is not intended to replace human controllers. Instead, the systems are designed to provide greater visibility and additional information to help controllers perform their existing duties.

“Our air traffic controllers continue to do the critical job of keeping aircraft safely separated, and we’re giving them better technology to do that,” said the FAA’s administrator, Bryan Bedford, in a statement.

“Digital towers provide controllers with greater visibility of airport activity and more information to make critical decisions,” he added.

Bedford is scheduled to appear before the House transportation and infrastructure committee next week, where he will face questions about the progress and challenges surrounding the administration’s ongoing $12.5bn modernization initiative.

The effort aims to replace decades-old equipment still used throughout the aviation system, including copper telecommunications lines, floppy disks and paper strips used to track aircraft.

Congress approved $12.5bn over five years in June 2025 to support air traffic control reforms, but the Trump administration is seeking another $30bn from the legislative branch to fund additional improvements.

Concerns about the types of technology being implemented within air traffic control have been gaining traction alongside the increasing unease about artificial intelligence as a whole. In September, the FAA rolled out a new AI software tool called the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (Smart).

Trump has been heavily criticized for his response to a national shortage of air traffic controllers following last year’s government shutdown.

Staffing levels in control towers and many related aspects of US air traffic safety systems have been under especially close scrutiny since a midair collision between a passenger jet and a military helicopter on the outskirts of Washington DC in 2025 that killed 67 people. It was the deadliest crash in the US for more than 20 years and the authorities later deemed it “100% preventable”.

articles.title: Pro-trans activists hold rally against Washington state ballot initiative to protect girls sports
articles.excerpt: Four states voted on ballot measures to ban transgender athletes from women's sports in the 2026 midterm elections. The measures passed in Arizona and Nebraska, while results in Colorado and Washingto...
articles.body_text:
Four states voted on ballot measures to ban transgender athletes from women's sports in the 2026 midterm elections. The measures passed in Arizona and Nebraska, while results in Colorado and Washington remain pending.

Transgender-rights supporters marched through downtown Seattle Thursday after Washington voters approved a measure barring biological males from girls’ K–12 interscholastic sports, setting up a potential court battle over the new restrictions.

Demonstrators gathered at Westlake Park before marching toward Pike Place Market, according to KUOW. The protest followed the passage of Initiative 638, which also requires students seeking to compete in girls’ sports to provide medical verification of their biological sex.

The measure had 56.8% support in returns reported Thursday by FOX 13 Seattle. The Associated Press called its passage Wednesday evening, with ballots still being counted.

WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS APPEAR TO PASS FIRST-EVER BALLOT MEASURE SEPARATING BOYS AND GIRLS SPORTS

"I was kind of expecting it, but it was still devastating nonetheless," Evan Gortner of Gender Equity Movement, which organized the protest, told KUOW.

Marchers chanted, "638 is trans hate." Some attendees also criticized Democratic leaders for not doing more to defeat the initiative.

The result delivered a victory to Let’s Go Washington, the conservative group behind the measure, even as voters rejected two other initiatives it backed concerning parental rights and the repeal of the state’s tax on high earners.

Supporters argue that separating girls’ sports by biological sex protects fairness, safety and athletic opportunities for female students. Opponents contend the restrictions discriminate against transgender students and could subject girls to intrusive medical verification.

WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE

The dispute now extends beyond the election results.

Gender Justice League Executive Director Danni Askini told KUOW her organization was consulting partners and evaluating a possible challenge on student-privacy grounds. The group had not formally announced a lawsuit in that Nov. 5 report.

The ACLU of Washington also condemned the outcome, but told KUOW it does not discuss potential litigation. That response did not announce a lawsuit.

Washington Democrats, meanwhile, have said they support other organizations pursuing challenges but will not bring a case themselves.

"WA Dems will not be challenging the initiative in court. We believe there will be organizations who do and we support those efforts," the party previously told OutKick.

Party Chair Shasti Conrad called the initiative unconstitutional in a Nov. 5 statement.

The measure’s medical-verification requirement has become a central point of contention.

Its text requires a health examination and consent form, or another statement signed by a student’s personal healthcare provider, verifying biological sex as part of the required routine sports physical. That verification must rely on reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels. The text does not prescribe a particular examination or test.

Washington has allowed students to compete on teams consistent with their gender identity since 2007.

The debate also prompted protests from female athletes before the election. About a dozen Camas girls declined to race against a transgender teammate on Oct. 13, OutKick previously reported.

For schools, the immediate question is how to carry out the new requirements.

The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association told KUOW it was preparing changes for Dec. 3 and reviewing implementation, including physical-examination requirements. It said updated guidance and forms would go to schools after legal review.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

Israel’s president has ⁠chosen Gadi Eisenkot, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠stro...
articles.body_text:
Knesset has been deadlocked since the election last month when Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority

Israel’s president has ⁠chosen Gadi Eisenkot, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠strongest rival, to ⁠try to ​form a new government, after a deadlocked election that left neither man ⁠with a clear path to power.

Isaac Herzog’s office said he had informed Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, on Saturday night “of his intention to task him with forming a government”.

It added that the formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony on Sunday at the president’s residence in Jerusalem.

Netanyahu ‌is fighting to hold on to office ‌after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an election on 27 October but still emerged as the largest bloc ‌in parliament.

Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a coalition, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier.

Eisenkot’s wide-ranging opposition bloc won 48 of the Israeli parliament’s 120 seats in October elections, while Netanyahu’s camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.

During party consultations with Herzog, 66-year-old Eisenkot received the endorsements of both Arab-majority lists, who could now play kingmakers after making unprecedented gains in the vote.

But it remains unclear if Eisenkot’s bloc would accept support from the Arab lists in forming a government.

Eisenkot, the military chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has set out to unite Israelis after Netanyahu’s divisive tenure, under which the country moved sharply to the right.

He has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity, decrying recent incidents as “Jewish terror” abetted by Netanyahu’s government.

But the military man is no peacenik. He opposes the creation of a Palestinian state and vowed to end Hamas’s rule in Gaza and destroy the Islamist movement’s military wing.

Commanding the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah, Eisenkot devised the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”. The idea, named after a Beirut suburb heavily damaged in that war, involves Israel vowing to use massive force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Lebanese militant movement Hezbollah.

articles.title: Trump orders DOJ to investigate Democrats for ‘threatening’ people
articles.excerpt: United States President Donald Trump has ordered the ⁠⁠Department of Justice (DOJ) to look into Democrats ‌‌for “threatening a lot of people” with impeachment and other ⁠⁠forms of ⁠⁠punishment, follow...
articles.body_text:
United States President Donald Trump has ordered the ⁠⁠Department of Justice (DOJ) to look into Democrats ‌‌for “threatening a lot of people” with impeachment and other ⁠⁠forms of ⁠⁠punishment, following their midterm election victory.

In a Truth Social post on Saturday, Trump said what Democrats had done amounted to a “criminal act”, without providing evidence.

The post comes days after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress from Republicans in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democratic lawmakers and newly elected candidates have said they would pursue probes into the Trump family’s financial dealings, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), as well as investigations into Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump wrote, adding that some of his cabinet have been threatened with impeachment. “This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable for this.”

Trump also said, without evidence, that some Democrats were threatening his donors, whom he called “some of the most respected people anywhere in the World”. He said Democrats were targeting them for their political views, specifically calling out Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin. He gave no evidence of her threatening people over their views.

When Democrats take control of Congress in January, they will be able to conduct a range of investigations, in which they can order access to documents, summon Trump officials to testify, and hold hearings.

Democratic Representative Robert Garcia of California, who is likely to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, which serves as the investigative committee in the House and has broad jurisdiction and power, posted “LAWYER UP” on social media after it was clear Democrats would take the House.

During his second term, Trump has called for investigations into his political enemies, including the former director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), James Comey, and New York Attorney General Letitia James.
