Bill Belichick, the day his UNC T...
articles.body_text:
"The shtick is up. They're getting tired of the off-field noise, overseeing the stuff that they're trying to do on the field. This is turning into an embarrassment."

Bill Belichick, the day his UNC Tar Heels were set to face the No. 1 Miami Hurricanes in Chapel Hill, was the center of more off-field noise regarding his relationship.

This time, though, it was reported the 74-year-old actually ended things with 25-year-old Jordon Hudson over a year ago, per TMZ. They remain "committed to their business partnerships" and "remain close friends."

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Nonetheless, a game had to be played, and Belichick and UNC were certainly not thinking about his relationship status. They wanted to give Miami a run for their money.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Head coach Bill Belichick of the North Carolina Tar Heels looks on before a game against the Syracuse Orange at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, N.C., on Oct. 24, 2026. (Getty Images)

The Tar Heels came close to upsetting the Hurricanes, but they ran out of gas in the fourth quarter in a 38-35 loss to move to 4-4 on the season. Miami stayed undefeated, improving to 8-0 on the year and 6-0 in ACC play.

No one expected Belichick's squad to be able to handle the Hurricanes, led by Mario Cristobal. But just as Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah continued his efficient play this season, Billy Edwards Jr. was matching him when the Tar Heels had the ball.

Edwards threw for 341 yards on 28-of-34 through the air with four touchdown passes, including a 16-yard strike to Jordan Shipp to take a 21-17 lead — UNC’s first of the game — in the third quarter.

From there, both teams were trading blows, and the lead, on the scoreboard. Miami responded with an 80-yard drive to retake their lead, 24-21, but UNC continued to fight on while crushing clock heading into the fourth quarter.

Edwards led a 16-play, 75-yard drive capped with a touchdown run by Demon June from one yard out. There was a lot of time left in this ballgame, which Miami knew despite some shock of what UNC was doing to them at home.

Mensah wasn’t fazed, though, as yet another touchdown drive came from the Hurricanes thanks to key catch-and-runs, including a 31-yard burst from star receiver Malachi Toney. Mark Fletcher Jr. regained the Miami lead with a two-yard run and 7:49 left on the clock.

The way this game was going, it seemed Belichick and UNC would have a chance if they were able to get the ball last. However, a grave error slammed the door shut on those chances.

Edwards was strip-sacked by Marquise Lightfoot, and Miami recovered at the UNC 37-yard line. That was the defensive stop needed to swing the tides of momentum, and Mensah didn’t thwart that opportunity.

The third try was finally recovered by the Hurricanes, and they ran the clock out.

Mensah threw for 274 yards and three scores, while rushing for 36 yards. Toney had two of those touchdowns, hauling in seven receptions for 75 yards. Fletcher also scored three total touchdowns.

articles.title: Ukrainian evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunite with family
articles.excerpt: Starved and exhausted residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky have crossed into Ukraine in a major evacuation operation of civilians, under the first humanitarian truce of its kind...
articles.body_text:
Starved and exhausted residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky have crossed into Ukraine in a major evacuation operation of civilians, under the first humanitarian truce of its kind in more than four years of Moscow’s war.

The six-day ceasefire covering the town was reached with mediation efforts by US First Lady Melania Trump and help from Pope Leo XIV. It is the longest local pause in fighting since Russia’s full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022.

“Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky have crossed the Ukrainian border in the Chernihiv region. All of them will receive the assistance they need,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on X, thanking the United States and the first lady for mediating.

“Further steps toward de-escalation and real progress toward peace are also needed,” he added.

Evacuees wrapped in blue and yellow Ukrainian flags stepped off buses at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border and reunited with family members.

Ukrainian officials met the evacuees with posters reading “You’re not alone” and “We embrace with our hearts”, while residents from nearby villages lined the highway waving flags and flashlights to greet them.

Supply routes to Oleshky had been disrupted by fighting and drones. According to some residents, food deliveries were stopped in May, pushing hundreds of people into starvation.

One evacuee, an elderly man in a wheelchair, told the Reuters news agency that he had lost 20kg (44lbs) over the past year, becoming so weak he required hospital treatment.

Another evacuee, Svitlana Yermakova, told Reuters they had to eat grass to survive.

“We chopped grass and squash… just to hold on,” she said, adding that she risked riding by bicycle through minefields to a nearby village to get food for herself and her dog.

To reach Ukrainian-held territory, Oleshky residents had to take a complicated route to leave the devastated town just a few kilometres from the front line.

They first crossed Crimea by bus to the Russian town of Anapa before flying to Belarus, from where they crossed into Ukraine.

Ambulances lined the street, and several large military tents were erected, where hot meals, tea and medical aid were provided.

Russian and Ukrainian officials say the ceasefire in Oleshky has held since Tuesday, allowing them to de-mine the roads and bring food, medicines and other supplies into the town again.

The truce is due to end on Sunday evening.

Some residents have decided to remain in Oleshky, despite the ongoing lack of gas, electricity and running water.

Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said living conditions in the occupied Oleshky remained difficult, pledging she would continue to work with her Ukrainian counterpart, Dmytro Lubinets, to help those who stayed.

“The mission has come to an end,” she said on Telegram. “We have agreed to carry out regular humanitarian missions, which is a very important step.”

Oleshky had a pre-war population of about 24,000, which plunged to an estimated 1,700 before the evacuation.

Ukrainian officials have not said exactly how many residents were evacuated or how many remained.

Despite the ceasefire in Oleshky, fighting rages on in other parts of the front, with Russia and Ukraine keeping up drone attacks against each other.

TRANSFER PORTAL, NOT NIL, REASON FOR PARITY, CLAIMS COLLEGE FOOTBALL EXPERT BROOKS AUSTIN

BYU wide receiver Kyler Kasper scores a touchdown during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Arizona State on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Provo, Utah. (AP Photo/Tyler Tate)

articles.title: Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream fall short in Game 7 as Golden State Valkyries win first WNBA championship
articles.excerpt: Prior to Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players leave the floor before the national anthem. The players left the floor during the national anthem for all seven gam...
articles.body_text:
Prior to Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players leave the floor before the national anthem. The players left the floor during the national anthem for all seven games.

SAN FRANCISCO – Angel Reese scored one point and did not attempt a field goal in the fourth quarter of Game 7. The Atlanta Dream needed more from her with a championship on the line.

The Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta 68-63 on Saturday night at Chase Center, winning the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 4-3 to claim the franchise’s first championship.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Reese finished with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, 12 rebounds and four turnovers. It was her fourth consecutive game with more turnovers than made field goals. Across those four games, she shot 12-for-45 (26.7%) and committed 19 turnovers.

USA SPORTS, NBC CLAIM RECORD WNBA FINALS RATINGS, BUT COMPARISONS LEAVE OUT IMPORTANT CONTEXT

Angel Reese scored just one fourth-quarter point in Game 7 as Gabby Williams erupted for 30 points to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a title. (Getty Images)

Golden State guard Gabby Williams delivered the performance Atlanta needed from its star. She was named Finals MVP after scoring 30 points, including 28 in the second half, and blocking four shots in the clincher. Her 31-foot three-pointer with 2:18 remaining broke a 57-57 tie and put Golden State ahead for good.

Reese’s only point in the final period came on a free throw with 18.6 seconds remaining.

Before tipoff, both teams again left the court for the national anthem, completing the seven-game series without appearing on the floor for any of the performances.

WNBA FINALS TEAMS END SEASON WITH ONE FINAL NATIONAL ANTHEM SNUB AS DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT

Reese’s Finals had looked much different when Atlanta held a 2-1 series lead.

She combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Games 2 and 3, then explained how she believed she was getting into Golden State’s head.

"They’re playing into my mental game where I can take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up," Reese said before Game 4.

Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream reacts during Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center. (Getty Images)

The Valkyries won the next two games. Atlanta forced Game 7 with an 80-69 victory Thursday behind Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard’s combined 44 points, but Reese continued to struggle with her shooting, making five of 18 attempts.

She finished the final four games with 38 points, 13 fewer than she scored in Games 2 and 3 combined.

Saturday offered a chance to finish the series differently. Instead, Jordin Canada carried Atlanta’s offense for much of the night, while Reese never became a scoring factor down the stretch.

The Dream went scoreless for the first 5:19 as Golden State built an 8-0 lead. Reese finally put Atlanta on the board with a basket off an offensive rebound.

Atlanta recovered to trail just 14-12 after one quarter, and Reese’s three-pointer early in the second gave the Dream their first lead.

Canada scored 11 points in the second quarter and had 13 at halftime. Golden State went more than eight minutes without a field goal to begin the period, allowing Atlanta to take a 30-24 lead into the break.

Reese had five points, seven rebounds and three turnovers at halftime. Williams had just two points.

The Dream extended their lead to 37-28 midway through the third quarter. Then Williams took over.

She scored Golden State’s final 13 points of the period, including three three-pointers in a 56-second span. Reese answered one of those threes with a hook through contact, but missed the accompanying free throw. It was her last basket of the night.

Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries won WNBA Finals MVP after scoring 30 points in Game 7. (Getty Images)

Williams’ turnaround jumper with 1:05 remaining gave the Valkyries a 45-44 lead entering the fourth. She scored 15 points in the quarter and added 13 more in the final period.

Allisha Gray’s two free throws tied the game at 55 with 3:15 left. Williams answered with a driving layup. Howard tied it again at 57 before Williams buried the three from 31 feet.

After Gray missed a wide-open layup, Williams made two free throws to push Golden State’s lead to five with 1:40 remaining.

Kiah Stokes then delivered on the offensive glass. She rebounded two consecutive Williams misses, converting the second into a putback that stretched the lead to 64-57 with 53.8 seconds left.

Gray’s three-pointer brought Atlanta within four, but Tiffany Hayes answered with two free throws.

Reese grabbed an offensive rebound and drew a foul with 18.6 seconds remaining. She missed the first free throw and made the second, leaving Atlanta down five.

Angel Reese No. 5 of the Atlanta Dream reacts after scoring a basket and drawing a foul during the third quarter in Game 7 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center on Oct. 31, 2026, in San Francisco, Calif. (Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

She then stole a Williams pass, and Gray made two free throws to cut the deficit to 66-63 with 10.5 seconds left. Veronica Burton’s two free throws with 5.1 seconds remaining secured the victory.

Stokes finished with eight points, 13 rebounds and two blocks. Burton added 10 points and 11 rebounds, while Hayes scored 11.

Canada led Atlanta with 18 points, and Gray added 16. Howard finished with six points on 3-for-14 shooting, missing all seven of her three-point attempts. The Dream shot 33.3% overall and went 6-for-30 from beyond the arc.

Reese finished the series averaging 14.7 points and 12.9 rebounds while shooting 40.5% from the field.

After Game 3, she had explained how she measures greatness.

"I think you become one of the greats … when you can win and impact winning," Reese said.

She helped put Atlanta two wins from a championship. Across the final four games, she didn't do enough for the Dream to finish the job.

articles.title: Binance says 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack covered as FBI says North Korea behind attack
articles.excerpt:
Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals expected to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠a...
articles.body_text:
Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals expected to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea.

The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.

Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said in its latest update that it was on track to resume them on Sunday.

The announcement came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.

It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets”.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses.

“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said ​on X.

The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

The FBI has linked North Korea to the theft of a record $6.3bn in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance.

Malicious actors from North Korea were observed laundering the ⁠stolen assets ⁠by converting them primarily into the cryptocurrency Ethereum, ⁠the FBI said in a statement on Saturday.

The US agency blamed the operation specifically on a group called TraderTraitor, the same group blamed for a $1.5bn theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.

According to the statement, the assets are expected to be “further laundered” in stages.

The FBI called on virtual asset service providers to block transactions being used in the latest laundering operation, providing the suspected digital addresses to watch for.

In a separate statement on Saturday, Binance said it has replaced 90 percent of the amount stolen by using company money to buy new tokens.

The remaining 10 percent consists of less liquid tokens, meaning they ⁠may take longer to buy, it added.

“We will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets… until the covered amount reaches 100 [percent] for all tokens. Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users,” the company said on X.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from a $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a Bitcoin reserve fund Binance ⁠holds to protect customers in the event of security ⁠breaches, as well as some of its Futures Insurance Fund and the company’s corporate treasury.

Crypto prices fell on Friday, as Binance, which runs the world’s largest crypto exchange, sought to reassure customers their funds were safe.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to ⁠delete evidence of its activity, making it hard to trace and investigate.

After ⁠the hack, the exchange stopped allowing customers to withdraw their funds.

Binance said later on Saturday that it was on track to reopen withdrawals on Sunday.

Binance also announced the publication of a new proof-of-reserves snapshot, allowing users to independently verify that their assets were backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio.

articles.title: Paul Skenes and Livvy Dunne's Halloween costume will enrage anyone tired of rushing through holidays
articles.excerpt:
Cal tries to loosen up by putting on a Halloween costume, but gets annoyed when his listeners have no clue who he is supposed to be.

I hope you had a great Halloween. I know I did, handing out candy ...
articles.body_text:
Cal tries to loosen up by putting on a Halloween costume, but gets annoyed when his listeners have no clue who he is supposed to be.

I hope you had a great Halloween. I know I did, handing out candy to the two trick-or-treaters who stopped at my house.

And to the kids who walked by my house without stopping, the joke is on you: I now have a giant bowl of Twizzlers, Reese's and Jolly Ranchers to shame-eat for the next couple of days.

And plenty of athletes seemed to have a great holiday too, including Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes and his girlfriend Livvy Dunne.

CARDINALS' BUDDA BAKER FIELDS QUESTIONS ABOUT TRADE RUMORS WHILE WEARING EVIL CLOWN HALLOWEEN MASK

Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes and Livvy Dunne walk the red carpet for the MLB All-Star Game on July 14, 2026, in Philadelphia. (Chris Szagola/AP Photo)

But their costume choice is alarming for those of us who want to savor Halloween before we start looking not one, but two holidays ahead.

The couple shared photos and video of their costumes: Buddy the Elf of "Elf" fame and a bottle of Mrs. Butterworth's syrup.

It's a solid costume, as Will Ferrell's iconic character is big on syrup, but... CHRISTMAS?!?!

Like, not even Neal Page and Del Griffith from "Planes, Trains, and Automobiles" would tell Halloween to pound sand, skip Thanksgiving like some soulless red-headed holiday stepchild and go straight to Christmas.

It kind of reminds me of a Halloween I had a couple of years ago. I was working in my office that afternoon and watching 1933's "The Invisible Man" when I heard my wife digging for something in the closet.

MAGGIE SAJAK LOOKS LIKE A MILLION BUCKS FOR HALLOWEEN, BILLY NAPIER MAKES HORRIBLE HISTORY & TIM DUNCAN VOTES!

Moments later, she walked out with our Christmas tree and set it up before the Invisible Man even left the Lion's Head Inn.

I'm not a hard-and-fast "Christmas must wait until after-Thanksgiving" guy. I'll hum a Christmas carol or steal a mini candy cane from a bank teller's desk before Thanksgiving Day, but I never go full-Christmas until I awake from my Thanksgiving food coma.

Paul Skenes of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches the selection show with his girlfriend Olivia Dunne during the ROY 2024 National League Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year Award Announcement on Monday, Nov. 18, 2024 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Lucas Casel/MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Not Skenes and Dunne, though. They’re already in Christmas mode while people across the country are still dressing as the woman from "Obsession," donning inflatable Minion costumes and waiting to take their first Halloween Jell-O shot.

I mean, great costume work, but let's savor Halloween before we have to start thinking about buying everyone in our family Amazon gift cards.

articles.title: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.excerpt:
Thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv to urge the Israeli opposition to make a deal with Arab parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Protesters at Saturday’s rally told the AFP n...
articles.body_text:
Thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv to urge the Israeli opposition to make a deal with Arab parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Protesters at Saturday’s rally told the AFP news agency this may be the “last chance for real change” and that Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, is a “great manipulator”.

Main opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has previously ruled out forming a coalition with Israel’s Arab parties, but a deadlock in Tuesday’s elections means siding with the parties could help him form a government.

“People really want this vote for change to work out, and they believe that… Gadi Eisenkot and other leaders of the Jewish-Israeli parties need to listen to their voice,” Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh said from Ramallah on Saturday.

Counter-protesters also showed up to Saturday’s demonstrations, with Netanyahu supporters seen shouting their own demands that “Israel should not have a government with so-called terrorists”, Odeh said.

Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s elections, while Eisenkot’s won 48, meaning neither side can form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament alone.

Israel’s three Arab-led parties won 19 seats, having made significant gains in Tuesday’s election.

Nearly 840,000 people voted for Ra’am and the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-led parties, a 64 percent increase from the last elections in 2022, according to the Central Election Committee.

The Arab electoral success means a coalition with Eisenkot would provide a comfortable majority of 67. However, for many in Israel, the idea of siding with Arabs is politically unpalatable.

Netanyahu has accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it. Qatar has rejected the allegations, calling it a disinformation campaign.

Odeh said that Israeli right-wing circles have described “the historic turnout of Palestinian Israelis as electoral terrorism, equating it to the October 7th attack”, when Hamas-led fighters stormed southern Israel, killing more than 1,200 people and taking hundreds captive.

“Palestinian-Israeli votes and voices” are under attack because they have a “prominent position” in deciding whether Eisenkot can form a government, she added.

articles.title: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
articles.excerpt:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.

Besides Frank...
articles.body_text:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who targeted emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands earlier joined the demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.

The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police, AFP news agency reported. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".

She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."

Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?

Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe

While protests during the day were largely peaceful, the demonstrations turned violent as night fell.

In a post on X, Frankfurt police said that "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.

In later updates, officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.

Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds – looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

articles.title: Cruise company founder says he's 'the villain' after 200-plus passengers are stranded
articles.excerpt: A cruise promising passengers a lifetime at sea came to an abrupt halt in Cambodia after soaring fuel costs made the voyage too expensive to continue. Passengers who had spent months living aboard the...
articles.body_text:
A cruise promising passengers a lifetime at sea came to an abrupt halt in Cambodia after soaring fuel costs made the voyage too expensive to continue. Passengers who had spent months living aboard the Villa Vie Odyssey said they were given just seven hours' notice to leave the ship.

The captain of the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship is speaking out after 203 residents were forced to disembark in Cambodia due to a critical fuel shortage, calling the ordeal "really painful."

The ship, which offered passengers the chance to make the ocean their permanent home, suspended its around-the-world voyage earlier this week after soaring fuel costs made continued operations financially unsustainable, according to its operator.

Residents were forced to leave the vessel in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, just two years after the ship set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, on what was supposed to be a 3 1/2-year journey around the world.

THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD

"I feel awful. They’re counting on me to make the decisions here, and there’s nothing else I’m focused on. I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents [with] a solution," Mikael Petterson, founder and executive chairman of Villa Vie Residences, told Business Insider.

Some residents had paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the chance to live aboard.

The Villa Vie Odyssey had marketed its around-the-world journey as an alternative to traditional retirement, offering residents the opportunity to live permanently at sea. (AFP via Getty Images)

Villa Vie Residences had offered lifetime access to the ship through its "Endless Horizons" program for a one-time payment of $299,999 for a single-occupancy cabin or $499,999 for double occupancy, Fox Business reported in May 2024.

Captain Emanuele Giudice on Thursday opened up about what led to the decision to force residents off the ship.

"Unfortunately, due to the shortage of fuel, we needed to shut down one generator, chiller, non-essential lights," Giudice said, as Reuters reported.

CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE

Giudice said the shutdowns would have "created discomfort to the residents, which — we don't want that."

"So we kindly asked the residents to get off the ship because our fuel situation was critical," he said.

"There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."

Asked who was to blame, Giudice pointed to high fuel prices, saying they had significantly affected the ship's travel.

CRUISE FEE DOUBLES AT VACATION HOT SPOT AS PASSENGERS BRACE FOR EVEN STEEPER HIKES

He declined to comment when a reporter asked whether the war in the Middle East and President Donald Trump were responsible.

Giudice also said residents were given more than 24 hours' notice to leave the ship. Yet passengers previously told The Associated Press (AP) they received just seven hours' notice and had to make their own accommodations.

The cruise ship suspended its around-the-world voyage after soaring fuel costs left its operator unable to financially sustain continued operations. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)

Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, previously told AP they were repeatedly asked for fuel money.

"I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents on a solution."

"We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," Lynn Montoya said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole," she added.

Benjamin Schatz, a retiree who had hoped to make the MV Odyssey his forever home, told CBS News he was devastated after being forced to leave the ship.

Villa Vie Odyssey Capt. Emanuele Giudice, seen at center, said a critical fuel shortage forced the crew to shut down certain systems aboard the ship. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)

"Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz said, as CBS reported.

He added, "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."

The company had marketed life aboard the Odyssey as an alternative to traditional retirement, appealing to retirees concerned about inflation, rising living expenses and the possibility of outliving their savings.

Petterson promoted the experience as a way for retirees to live on a fixed budget without worrying about ongoing expenses.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"For less than the price of an average home, you can secure a lifetime of experiences," Petterson said at the time.

Residents of the Villa Vie Odyssey seen above were forced to leave the cruise ship in Cambodia after its operator said continued operations were financially unsustainable. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to Villa Vie Residences for comment.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed reporting.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

articles.title: Transfer portal, not NIL, reason for parity, claims college football expert Brooks Austin
articles.excerpt:
College football expert Brooks Austin claims the transfer portal is to blame for parity in the sport, not NIL.

It's no secret that college football has seen its fair share of parity over the past few...
articles.body_text:
College football expert Brooks Austin claims the transfer portal is to blame for parity in the sport, not NIL.

It's no secret that college football has seen its fair share of parity over the past few years.

A sport that was once dominated by the SEC, more specifically Alabama, has become completely wide open in terms of legitimate championship contenders.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

It all culminated in a team like Indiana, one of the worst programs in college football history, completing a 16-0 dream season with a national championship just last year.

SEC'S CRAZY, HISTORY-MAKING WEEK 7 WEEKEND IS THE LATEST EXAMPLE OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S NEW ERA

Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza passes against Miami during the first half of the College Football Playoff national championship game, Monday, Jan. 19, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Now in 2026, the parity has reached an all-time high, with no truly dominant team standing out eight weeks into the season.

Many fans and pundits alike have attributed this to the advent of NIL, and their reasoning is fairly sound.

Of course, the proliferation of talent would become "flatter" when every program is allowed to legally pay money for players.

Not everyone is on board with this theory, though, and one of the voices leading the charge in the opposite direction is none other than "The Film Guy," Brooks Austin.

In an exclusive interview with OutKick, Austin reasoned that it's actually the transfer portal, and not NIL, that is the cause for all this chaos in the ranks of CFB.

"Everybody blames it on NIL," he explains. "I think it has far more to do with freedom of movement. The portal has changed this more than anything else."

As Austin puts it, teams like Bama and Georgia can no longer stack talent and stick it on the proverbial shelf for three years.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) rolls out of the pocket against Alabama during the second half of a Southeastern Conference championship NCAA college football game, Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

"Georgia can pay their backup just as much as Wake Forest can pay him to be a starter... so when a backup defensive tackle has been sitting on the bench for 2 years, he wants to play."

Money is a factor, according to Austin, but it has just as much to do with the disappearance of depth as it does with overall funding.

"I think NIL has certainly created some of this parity and created opportunities for dispersion of talent," he says. "But I think a lot of it also has to do with the fact that we're actually able to transfer, we're able to go."

A perfect example is when the aforementioned Bulldogs and Crimson Tide met in the 2025 SEC Championship Game.

Parker Brailsford (72) of the Alabama Crimson Tide prepares to snap the ball against the Georgia Bulldogs during the first quarter in the 2025 SEC Championship at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Dec. 06, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

"I remember last year in the SEC championship game, Georgia's down several starters on the offensive line, and Alabama is down several starters on their defensive line," Austin recalls. "I remember that same situation happening in 2022 before the portal got absolutely rampant and Georgia loses the starting left tackle and it's like, OK, don't worry. Here's Broderick Jones. He's a former five-star and he hasn't been playing at all, he's gonna go block Will Anderson for four quarters."

"And, you know, Broderick. I don't know if he stays around for 2 years to sit on the bench nowadays, right?"

A combination of NIL and the transfer portal is certainly proving to be the great equalizer in college football, but it's fairly clear one has a lot more to do with it than the other.

articles.title: Syracuse stuns SMU 30-27 with a go-ahead touchdown with 17 seconds left for Halloween upset
articles.excerpt: This has to be one of the scariest Halloweens on record for SMU fans, after a shocking loss to Syracuse has seriously hurt their shot at an ACC Championship Game appearance, and may have also ended th...
articles.body_text:
This has to be one of the scariest Halloweens on record for SMU fans, after a shocking loss to Syracuse has seriously hurt their shot at an ACC Championship Game appearance, and may have also ended their chance at a College Football Playoff appearance.

The Mustangs headed to central New York as the No. 19 team in the nation with some serious buzz around them potentially making it to the playoffs come the end of the season.

However, the Orange — a fitting team to pull off a Halloween upset — had other ideas, winning this one 30-27.

MORE QUESTIONS THAN ANSWERS: ARCH MANNING LIKES THE DISRESPECT, BIG 12'S DISASTER AND A CFP RACE IN DISARRAY

Syracuse quarterback Steve Angeli scores a touchdown during the first half against SMU. (AP Photo/Adrian Kraus)

One of SMU's big problems on the day involved its offensive line.

Quarterback Kevin Jennings continued his strong season with a whopping 351 passing yards and two touchdowns.

However, there may have been some more that got away, as the Mustangs allowed the Orange to sack him six times, including once with seconds on the clock as SMU worked to get into field goal range.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Meanwhile, Syracuse's Steve Angeli was good for 200 yards and a rushing touchdown, but none of it was as big as the go-ahead touchdown.

With just 17 seconds left on the clock, Angeli hit tight end Noah Meyers to give Syracuse the lead.

There was still time for SMU to potentially send this one to overtime, but an incomplete pass, the aforementioned sixth sack of the day, and a bizarre final play that went nowhere and resulted in a fumble meant Syracuse had secured the upset.

You've got to love a Halloween field-storming. With Big Bird, Ninja Turtles, and more swarming the field, it always feels a bit like a fever dream.

Fans run on the field after Syracuse beat No. 19 SMU in a stunning, Halloween upset. (AP Photo/Adrian Kraus))

That was SMU's second loss of the season, the first of which came just three games into the season against Louisville.

While a 6-2 record is solid, a loss to an unranked team that came in under .500 is going to be a tough sell for the CFP committee.

articles.title: USA Sports and NBC claim record WNBA Finals ratings, but the comparisons leave out important context
articles.excerpt:
Before the WNBA Finals Game 6, Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players leave the floor before the national anthem.

USA Sports announced Saturday that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals averaged 1.5 m...
articles.body_text:
Before the WNBA Finals Game 6, Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players leave the floor before the national anthem.

USA Sports announced Saturday that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals averaged 1.5 million viewers on Thursday afternoon. I'll admit, that number raised my eyebrows.

A game that tipped off at 12:30 p.m. Eastern, or 9:30 a.m. in the morning in the Golden State Valkyries' home market, outdrew last year's championship clincher in primetime?

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

USA Sports says it did, by 4%. The release combines viewers across USA Network, E! and SYFY with streaming led by Peacock, but doesn't break out how much of the audience came from television or streaming.

WNBA BAILED OUT OF SCHEDULING DISASTER AS ANGEL REESE, DREAM FORCE GAME 7

WNBA Finals ratings claims from NBC and USA Sports need context as streaming totals and changes to Nielsen measurement complicate historical comparisons. (Adam Hagy/NBAE via Getty Images)

USA Sports and NBC Sports have been promoting record audiences throughout the Finals, with WNBA PR also distributing their releases through an NBA employee.

NBC called its 2.1 million audience for Game 1 the largest ever for a Finals opener. USA Sports touted Game 3's 1.71 million as the biggest Game 3 audience since 1999 and the highest ever on cable. Those figures, like the Game 6 announcement, combined television and streaming.

NBC called Game 4 between the Valkyries and Atlanta Dream the most-watched Game 4 in WNBA Finals history, reporting 1.9 million viewers across NBC and Peacock. The release touted a 14% increase over the previous record of 1.67 million for the New York Liberty and Minnesota Lynx on ESPN in 2024.

Keep in mind, ESPN requires paid access. NBC is available free over the air, and this year's game also had Peacock.

USA Sports says a Thursday afternoon WNBA Finals game outdrew last year's clincher, but its release leaves questions about the audience breakdown and measurement. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson)

According to Sports Media Watch, NBC's television audience was 1.66 million, slightly below the previous reported ESPN record. Another 232,000 came from streaming measured separately by Adobe Analytics. That addition put NBC's combined figure over the old mark, but NBC didn't include the breakdown in its release.

DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT BEFORE T.I.'S 10-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER SINGS WNBA FINALS ANTHEM

I wrote about this measurement issue in July, when CBS and NBC both claimed the season's biggest WNBA audience.

Even the Nielsen numbers come from different measurement systems. Nielsen made Big Data + Panel its standard in 2025, combining its household panel with information from smart TVs and set-top boxes across 45 million households. The 2024 ESPN figure predates that standard.

Nielsen also expanded its out-of-home measurement in 2025, increasing coverage from 66% to 100% of the contiguous U.S. television population, and it includes viewing in places such as bars and restaurants. Then, on Aug. 31 of this year, it introduced changes intended to better capture how many people watch together, using wearable devices that pick up television audio.

Nielsen says its changes are intended to improve accuracy and don't guarantee higher ratings. But if better measurement captures someone who was already watching the WNBA, that person isn't a new fan.

USA Sports promoted Monday's 1.4 million viewers across USA Network, CNBC and Peacock as the second-most-watched Finals Game 5 ever. Its release acknowledged that the 2024 Liberty-Lynx clincher held the record. What it didn't include was that game's audience: 2.15 million on ESPN, putting this year's reported total about 35% below it.

NBC's Game 4 television audience fell below ESPN's 2024 record, with streaming pushing the combined WNBA Finals figure above the previous mark. (Getty Images)

The 2024 Finals were a best-of-five series, making Game 5 a winner-take-all matchup for the championship. The WNBA expanded to best-of-seven in 2025, and this year's Game 5 began with the series tied 2-2, so neither team could clinch the title. Monday's game also faced Cowboys-Eagles on "Monday Night Football," which drew 18.8 million viewers, plus the World Series at 8.3 million and NBA regular-season games.

VALKYRIES PLAYER'S DAD PUTS WNBA ON BLAST FOR UNUSUAL FINALS START: 'LEAGUE'S FAULT'

The release did, however, highlight an 8% increase over Game 2. It also described Game 5 as the "third consecutive game that USA Sports has posted record viewership."

The releases cite Adobe Analytics for their streaming audiences, but they don't identify who independently verified those figures or provide the data behind them.

Adobe's documentation describes an average-minute audience calculation based on time spent watching divided by the content's duration or a selected reporting period. Its software lets customers choose reporting windows and, for certain calculations, whether viewing time includes commercials.

NBC's release doesn't specify those settings or explain how the streaming calculation was matched to its television measurement.

NBC and USA Sports cite Adobe Analytics for WNBA streaming audiences but don't explain how those figures were independently verified. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

Michael Mulvihill, Fox's president of insights and analytics, posted on X that Nielsen had told clients: "Mixing internal or third-party data with Nielsen metrics to make comparative statements in the press is not permissible." He added, "Hopefully this clear, fair policy will be rigorously enforced during football season."

NBC's own Sept. 14 release for the NFL season opener attributed its combined NBC and Peacock audience to "Nielsen Big Data inclusive of first party data." Its WNBA releases still combine Nielsen and Adobe figures. NBC should explain what independent verification applies to the WNBA streaming numbers and how its record claims fit Nielsen's policy.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

For Game 6, USA Sports cited Nielsen's "panel-only" data alongside Adobe Analytics. Its releases for Games 2, 3 and 5 used Nielsen's Big Data + Panel figures, plus Adobe.

Nielsen says Big Data + Panel figures generally take two to three days to arrive, and its press policy allows preliminary reporting for single-day events. So, the panel-only figure could be an early estimate while USA Sports waits for the final number. The Game 6 release doesn't say that, though. And it doesn't label the figure preliminary or explain the switch.

Game 6 was moved from 8 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. so it could be played at State Farm Arena, with the Hawks playing there that night. In announcing the move, the WNBA and NBA said they would join the broadcasters in a coordinated promotional push to get viewers to the new time slot. The move also took the game out of direct competition with "Thursday Night Football."

USA Sports has enough confidence in the figure to rank Game 6 as the fifth-most-watched WNBA Finals game on cable. Then it should be able to tell us whether the number is final and how much of it actually came from cable.

Kate Hudson told Fox News Digital that she is actively trying not to raise fame-obsessed children.

Dax Shepard confessed to flirting with an A-list actress despite knowing she was married at the time.

During a recent episode of his "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 51-year-old actor was discussing his friendship with guests Erin and Sara Foster and how they got close when he was dating actress Kate Hudson,

The conversation then shifted to how Shepard and Hudson became a couple, with the actor's co-host, Monica Padman, sharing he was "obsessed" with Hudson way before they got together.

"What happened was I was friends with Oliver. I f- - -ing adore Oliver. I was at his house one night playing poker and she came and played and she was still with Chris," he said. "I just thought she was so f- - -ing beautiful and I was like 'Oh my god I can't believe she's here.'"

Shepard admitted to flirting with Kate Hudson while she was still married. (Stewart Cook/CBS via Getty Images)

DAX SHEPARD SLAMMED FOR EXPOSING LATE ERIC DANE'S PRIVATE AA STRUGGLES AFTER DEATH

Despite knowing the actress was married, the podcast host said he "gave her everything I had in the reserve tank."

He recalled leaving that night thinking, "Well, that's as good of a job as one can do. She's married. Who cares?" and that he could walk away knowing he had "a great first showing."

Hudson was still married to Robinson when she met Shepard. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)

Following Hudson's separation from Chris Robinson, Shepard ran into her at a dinner hosted by their mutual friend, Steve Brill, and took his chance.

"Now she's single and I’m like, ‘Let’s see if we can f- - -ing muster up this magic and get it going again,’" he said. "And then I got it going again. And then from that night on we were just together every single day."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Shepard shared that once she was single, they reconnected at a Malibu dinner hosted by a mutual friend. (JB Lacroix/Getty Images)

The two dated for a few months in 2007 but remained friendly following their break-up.

During an appearance on his podcast in November 2019, Hudson and Shepard revealed that they initially were playing a joke on the paparazzi when they walked out of Nobu together holding hands, but then it ended up leading to something more.

"I was acting mad at the paparazzi that they were invading our privacy," Shepard explained. "And then it just somehow led to hanging out!"

"Then I wanted to have sex with him," Hudson added. "It was like the perfect move."

Shepard and Bell went on to tie the knot in 2013 and share two daughters. (Christopher Polk/2026GG/Penske Media via Getty Images)

After they went their separate ways, Shepard began dating actress Kristen Bell, who he tied the knot with in 2013. They now share two daughters, Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11.

Hudson was later engaged to Muse front man Matthew Bellamy from 2011 until they broke up in 2014. In their time together they welcomed one son, Bingham, 15, who joined Hudson's son Ryder, 22, from her relationship with Robinson.

She is now engaged to Danny Fujikawa, who she began dating in 2016. They share one child together, a daughter named Rani, 8.

Hudson and Fujikawa began dating in 2016. (Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images)

articles.title: No 13 Texas Tech takes down No 22 Arizona in Big 12, delivers the Wildcats a crushing blow to CFP hopes
articles.excerpt:
Cincinnati's Cole Tabb rushed for 58-yard TD run to seal the UPSET win over No. 8 Texas Tech.

Halloween just became a whole lot scarier for Arizona.

No. 13 Texas Tech (7-1) defeated No. 22 Arizona (...
articles.body_text:
Cincinnati's Cole Tabb rushed for 58-yard TD run to seal the UPSET win over No. 8 Texas Tech.

Halloween just became a whole lot scarier for Arizona.

No. 13 Texas Tech (7-1) defeated No. 22 Arizona (6-2) 34-26, delivering a massive blow to the Wildcats' College Football Playoff chances and Big 12 championship hopes. For Texas Tech, it was its 13th-straight win at home, which tied a program record.

After Texas Tech's loss to Cincinnati last week, head coach Joey McGuire benched quarterback Will Hammond for Thomas Castellanos, and the move paid off. Castellanos thrived with both his arm and his legs, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns while running for 117 yards and a touchdown. It was his fifth career game with more than 100 rushing yards.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Texas Tech's Thomas Castellanos runs with the ball against Arizona during a Big 12 Conference football game Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

The Texas Tech run game was fantastic, rolling up 332 yards in the win. Running back J'Koby Williams ran for 175 yards and a touchdown. However, it wasn't all great for the Red Raiders, as they fell behind early.

Both teams scored on their opening drives, with Arizona getting on the board first with a 35-yard field goal from kicker Michael Salgado-Medina. Texas Tech responded with a 13-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that was capped off with Castellanos' 24-yard touchdown pass to tight end Terrance Carter Jr. to put the Red Raiders up 7-3.

The two teams then traded punts and turnovers on downs before the Wildcats scored their first touchdown in epic fashion. On third-and-12 from their own 6-yard line, quarterback Noah Fifita dropped back into the end zone before scrambling to the sideline.

As he scrambled, Fifita threw a dart to Isaiah Mizell, who then turned on the afterburners and raced up the sideline for a 94-yard touchdown to put Arizona up 10-7.

The Wildcats then built on their lead coming out of the two-minute timeout in the second quarter with the Wildcat formation. Running back Kedrick Reescano took the direct snap and ran for the five-yard touchdown to finish the 14-play, 81-yard drive and put Arizona up 17-7.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Arizona running back Kedrick Reescano (3) scores a touchdown during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Texas Tech on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Lubbock, Texas. (AP Photo/Annie Rice)

The Red Raiders managed a field goal before the first half concluded to cut the deficit to seven, making it a 17-10 game.

Texas Tech built on its end-of-half momentum and scored on the opening drive of the third quarter to tie it 17-17. Castellanos faked a pitch outside before knifing through the Wildcats' defense for an eight-yard touchdown.

The Wildcats didn't blink, however, as they marched down the field with a 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that ended with Reescano punching the ball in from the 1-yard line for his second touchdown of the day. However, the Wildcats' extra-point attempt was blocked, so Arizona had just a 23-17 lead.

Texas Tech capitalized on the mistake, as on its second drive of the second half, it rifled down the field to score another third-quarter touchdown. On fourth-and-2 from the Arizona 27-yard line, Texas Tech decided to go for it on fourth down. Wide receiver Kenny Johnson ran a go route, and Castellanos found him for a touchdown.

Texas Tech tight end Terrance Carter Jr. (7) reaches for a touchdown pass over Arizona's Malcolm Hartzog Jr. during the first half of an NCAA college football game Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Lubbock, Texas. (AP Photo/Annie Rice)

Texas Tech nailed the extra point, going up 24-23. On defense, it shut down Arizona and kept its good vibes going, as kicker Stone Harrington made his second field goal of the day, a 42-yarder, to put Texas Tech up 27-23.

After trading scores to start the second half, the defenses started to show up.

Arizona's response to Texas Tech's field goal fell short, as it went for it on fourth-and-1 from Texas Tech's 18-yard line, but Fifita's pass was too high for tight end Tyler Powell.

Texas Tech, still up 27-23, had a chance to take a two-score lead but squandered it. Red Raiders running back Cameron Dickey fumbled, and Arizona recovered on Texas Tech's 43-yard line.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Texas Tech's Trey White celebrates a sack against Arizona during a Big 12 Conference football game Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

However, Arizona did not take advantage of the field position, as it was forced to punt. Yet, it forced a punt from Texas Tech to get the ball back with about four and a half minutes left.

Arizona then went three-and-out, as the Red Raiders' defense once again dominated the series and forced another punt, and then the offense took care of the rest.

On third-and-1, with Arizona needing just one more stop to get the ball back, Williams burst through a hole in the line and scored a 64-yard touchdown, putting the Red Raiders up 34-23. Williams' touchdown marked 17 unanswered points for the Red Raiders.

Arizona got a field goal late, but didn't convert the onside kick, sealing the crushing loss.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: District of Columbia and Virginia sue to block Trump’s triumphal arch plans
articles.excerpt:
The District of Columbia (DC) and the state of Virginia have filed a joint lawsuit to halt the construction of a large triumphal arch sought by United States President Donald Trump.

Filed on Saturday...
articles.body_text:
The District of Columbia (DC) and the state of Virginia have filed a joint lawsuit to halt the construction of a large triumphal arch sought by United States President Donald Trump.

Filed on Saturday, the lawsuit denounces the project as “flagrantly unlawful” and “legally indefensible”.

It calls on the federal court system to bar construction before it starts.

Otherwise, the lawsuit warns, Trump could claim that pausing construction already under way would pose a national security risk, as he has done with other controversial projects in the past.

“This is not the first time that Defendants have rushed to dramatically remake the District too quickly for courts to intervene,” the lawsuit reads. “This Court should not allow this effort to escape judicial scrutiny.”

Saturday’s complaint brings the total number of lawsuits against the arch to three.

Trump has championed the prospect of building a triumphal arch, similar to the Arc de Triomphe built in Paris during Napoleonic times.

Trump’s arch, however, is designed to stand 30 metres (100 feet) taller than the Statue of Liberty. It would tower from the Memorial Circle in Washington, DC, at 76 metres (250ft).

That colossal scale has prompted outrage, particularly from veterans’ groups who fear the arch would block views of Arlington National Cemetery, a hallowed military grave site.

White House officials maintain that ground could be broken as early as next week, on or around November 5.

On Friday, the administration unveiled a 106-page proposal for the arch to be a 12-storey megastructure, featuring a winged bronze statue of Lady Liberty lifting an eternal flame.

The arch would include two mezzanines and an observation deck with panoramic east-west views, as well as programme spaces, offices and a “fire command centre”.

Trump has previously said the arch would double as a military hub with snipers and drone capabilities.

Construction on the arch would also result in significant traffic changes in the area, including rerouting traffic to nearby roads.

In Saturday’s lawsuit, Attorneys General Brian Schwalb of Washington, DC, and Jay Jones of Virginia pointed to the project’s disruptive footprint as a major concern.

“As soon as defendants break ground on this project, they will inflict irreparable harm on both the District and Virginia,” the lawsuit said.

It warns that the anticipated three-year construction project will stymie commuter traffic, slow down emergency vehicles and generate significant pollution, including “stormwater runoff into the Potomac”.

The lawsuit calls on the court to force the Trump administration to get congressional authorisation before any construction can begin.

The new legal challenge comes on the heels of an October 8 filing by Arlington County, which was the first governmental body to mount a legal action against Trump’s planned monument.

In that lawsuit, the county’s governing board argued that the project would cause “significant harm” to its residents and likely require changes to nearby flight paths.

The first complaint came in February, when a group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian launched an effort to stop the arch.

District Judge Tanya Chutkan is overseeing that case, and she is weighing whether to issue a preliminary injunction to temporarily freeze any construction plans while the court hears arguments.

At a hearing on Friday, Chutkan deferred an immediate ruling but signalled that she would be issuing a decision expeditiously.

She previously ordered the administration to give the court 48 hours’ notice before undertaking any activities related to the construction of the arch.

The monument has already received early approval from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were all tapped by Trump.

articles.title: Kid Rock reveals what he told French President Macron after Trump unexpectedly handed him phone on golf course
articles.excerpt:
According to Kid Rock, a golf game with Donald Trump led to an unexpected chat with French President Emmanuel Macron after Trump handed him the phone. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

Musician Kid Rock d...
articles.body_text:
According to Kid Rock, a golf game with Donald Trump led to an unexpected chat with French President Emmanuel Macron after Trump handed him the phone. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

Musician Kid Rock drew laughs from comedian Bill Maher's audience as he recounted how a golf outing with President Donald Trump ended with the singer on the phone with French President Emmanuel Macron.

During Friday's episode of HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher," Kid Rock said he was golfing with Trump when the president handed him a phone with Macron on the line.

"That was funny. Yeah, we’re out golfing. I hate speaking out of school, but this is just a fun one," Kid Rock said.

He told Maher that Trump was taking calls throughout their golf outing.

DAVID MARCUS: BILL MAHER'S NO REPUBLICAN, HE'S JUST A RARE DEMOCRAT WHO THINKS

President Donald Trump, with singer Kid Rock by his side, speaks to reporters and signs an executive order related to enforcement in the concert and entertainment industry in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, DC, on March 31, 2025. (Jabin Botsford/The Washington Post via Getty Images)

"The guy’s taking calls all day," Kid Rock said. "He’s working while you’re golfing. This guy does not stop working. We can all agree on that. He sleeps maybe four or five hours a night. So we’re out there, Macron calls, we’re out there, [Trump’s] talking to him."

Kid Rock -- whose real name is Robert Ritchie -- then described how Trump handed him the phone while he stood beside the president's golf cart.

"We’re all standing there," Kid Rock continued. [Trump’s] like, ‘Hey, I’m here with the great Kid Rock,’ like Macron knows who I am, and he’s like, ‘Bob, say hello.’"

"So he gives me the phone and I’m like, ‘Hello, Mr. President,’" he added. "And I’m like, ‘I’m from the Paris of the Midwest: Detroit.’ And Trump leaves, he gets in the golf cart."

BILL MAHER FIRES BACK AT LIBERAL CRITICS OVER SECOND TRUMP DINNER

Comedian and television host Bill Maher arrived for the 27th Mark Twain Prize for American Humor gala at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts on June 28, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images)

Maher laughed as Kid Rock described the exchange, telling the audience, "He leaves Macron on the phone with Kid Rock."

Kid Rock concluded the story by mimicking his conversation with Macron, adding, "I was like, ‘So what else you been up to?'"

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

The musician’s recounting of the phone call drew laughs from Maher, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) and journalist Jim VandeHei.

The anecdote came during an episode in which Maher also fired back at a lengthy Truth Social post from Trump criticizing the comedian following their second White House dinner. Kid Rock and ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith also attended the dinner.

BILL MAHER RECOUNTS LARRY DAVID FALLING OUT, CELEBRITY BACKLASH AFTER TRUMP WHITE HOUSE DINNER

French President Emmanuel Macron meets with community members at a town hall on Oct. 23, 2026, in Trappes, France, following a shooting that killed one person and injured at least four others. France's National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office took over the investigation into the attack. (Hannah McKay/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"Eating with Trump is a lot like dating Taylor Swift," Maher said. "It’s a lot of fun at the time but later on, they’re tearing you a new a------."

Kid Rock’s story — and Maher’s apparent prompting — drew the ire of Democratic political strategist Kaivon Shroff, who told Fox News Digital the comedian’s knee-slapping was anything but candid.

"If Barack Obama had handed Emmanuel Macron off to some celebrity on a golf course and driven away, Maher would have gone on a ten-minute rant about how unserious, embarrassing and beneath the presidency it was," Shroff said. "Trump does it and suddenly Maher is pounding the table laughing like it is the funniest thing he has ever heard."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"So spare me the idea that this is some spontaneous, authentic reaction. It is a performance," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "He is putting on a show for the audience and trying to sell them on Trump as charming in a way he never would have tolerated from a Democratic president."

"His whole brand is the liberal who bashes other liberals," Shroff said. "But at some point if all you do is bash Democrats, pal around with Kid Rock, and suck up to Trump — you’re just a Republican."

Fox News Digital reached out to Maher for comment.

Julia Bonavita is a media and culture writer for Fox News Digital, and a Fox Flight Team drone pilot. You can follow her at @juliabonavita13 on all platforms and send story tips to julia.bonavita@fox.com.

articles.title: Arctic wolf attacks child during zookeeper event, girl airlifted to hospital
articles.excerpt:

An Arctic wolf attacked an 8-y...
articles.body_text:
National Park Service rangers cited a man who was seen on video approaching a pack of wild wolves at Yellowstone National Park. (Credit: Keith Allen Kerbs via Storyful)

An Arctic wolf attacked an 8-year-old girl during a special zookeeper event at a wildlife park, leaving her seriously injured.

The event took place Oct. 28 at Wildpark Johannismühle, located just outside the town of Baruth/Mark, Germany, which is about 45 miles south of Berlin, according to a news release from the Teltow-Fläming district.

While caretakers were giving water to the animals in the enclosure, the young girl was injured by "at least one wolf," a Brandenburg Police report said.

MAN CAUGHT ON CAMERA APPROACHING, SPRAYING UNKNOWN SUBSTANCE TOWARD YELLOWSTONE WOLVES: RANGER

The girl was treated by first responders before being airlifted to a hospital in Berlin.

Her condition has not been made public, but she sustained critical head injuries, local news outlet Bild reported.

An Arctic wolf (not pictured) recently attacked a young girl during a special zookeeper event at a wildlife park in Germany. (ullstein bild via Getty Images; iStock)

Two other girls were in the enclosure at the time, but the animal caretaker who was present took actions to protect them.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Chaplains are working with four people, including three children, to provide emotional support in the wake of the incident, the Teltow-Fläming news release said.

An investigation into the incident is underway.

Wildpark Johannismühle is home to both Arctic and gray wolves. (iStock)

The proper special authorities, which in this case include The Lower Nature Conservation Authority and the Veterinary and Food Surveillance Office, will be given a police report and determine next steps, according to the news release.

"The Veterinary and Food Surveillance Office will visit the wildlife park promptly and carry out an on-site animal welfare control," the release noted.

"A professional assessment of the health and behavior of the wolf, or of any wolves potentially involved, in connection with the incident is not yet available," it continued.

"Such assessments will be subject to further investigation."

Wildpark Johannismühle advertises multiple up-close encounters with animals.

The park advertises multiple up-close animal encounters for visitors to participate in during their visits.  (iStock)

During the park’s "Zookeeper for a Day" experiences, visitors can "maintain enclosures, prepare food, occupy and feed animals — and learn a lot of exciting background knowledge about our wildlife park residents," the website says. It calls the encounters "a look behind the scenes that normal visitors do not get."

"We very much hope that the child recovers soon."

It also says, "For our younger animal fans, we also offer the small animal caretaker day. Here, children can support the animal caretakers in their work for half a day (7:20 a.m.-1:30 p.m.), help and playfully get an exciting insight into everyday professional life — age-appropriate, supervised and with a lot of animal proximity."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Both Arctic and gray wolves inhabit the wildlife park, which will remain closed until Nov. 2, according to the website.

"We very much hope that the child recovers soon, and wish all those affected a lot of strength to process what they experienced," Björn Christian Paterok of the Teltow-Fläming district said in the news release.

Fox News Digital reached out to Wildpark Johannismühle for comment.

Sadie Chafe is a writer on the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

A man has been charged under the Explosives Act and Firearms Order after police searched properti...
articles.body_text:
The 35-year-old was charged after police searched properties in Shankill Road and Edwina Street areas

A man has been charged under the Explosives Act and Firearms Order after police searched properties in Belfast.

The 35-year-old was charged with offences including two counts of possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances, and possession of a prohibited weapon (discharge of electricity or noxious gas).

He is due to appear before Belfast magistrates court on Monday, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said.

The charges follow searches at properties in the Shankill Road and Edwina Street areas of north Belfast on Friday and Saturday.

DCI McCallum said: “Following these searches a number of suspicious devices, along with other items, were located and seized by officers for forensic examination.

“Local residents who were evacuated as a precaution have now been allowed to return home following the public safety operation conducted alongside ammunition technical officers.

“All cordons have now been lifted from the area, and we thank local residents for their patience as inquiries were conducted yesterday and into today.”

McCallum added: “As we continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident, we would appeal to anyone who may have information that could assist with inquiries to contact us on 101, quoting reference number 261 30/10/26.”
